title: The AI Skill Companies Now Hire For - Picking the Right Model
content:
Knowing how to prompt is not enough anymore.
The skill companies now pay for is picking the RIGHT model for each job.
Here is what happened yesterday.
OpenAI and Google Cloud announced that OpenAI models are coming to Google Cloud's Model Garden.
Three models are rolling out in private preview: GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol, and GPT-6 Luna.
And Google says it is now the only hyperscale cloud offering all three leading closed source model families, alongside more than two hundred other models.
Now read this line from Google's announcement.
Modern enterprise AI requires matching each workload to the right model, rather than relying on a single model for every task.
That sentence is a job description.
Think about what that means.
When every cloud offers hundreds of models, someone has to decide which one to use.
Someone has to test them, compare cost and speed, and explain the choice to the business.
That someone can be you.
So how do you show a recruiter you have this skill?
It takes one weekend.
Step ONE. Pick one real task, like answering support tickets.
Write twenty test questions with the answers you expect.
Step TWO. Run the same twenty questions through three models.
One big, one mid sized, and one fast and cheap.
Step THREE. Put the results in one simple table.
Accuracy, speed, and cost per thousand requests.
Then write one paragraph: which model you would pick, and why.
In an interview, when they ask how you would choose a model, you do not guess.
You show your table.
Imagine saying, "The cheapest model was good enough for eighty percent of tickets, so I would route only the hard ones to the big model."
That one line shows judgment, and judgment is what gets hired.
Here's my take. Models will keep changing every month.
The person who can test, compare, and explain will always have work.
Follow for your daily AI update.
